changes: Pass an allocation scope to one-shot physical aggregate fallback execution.
Retain the next snapshot before releasing the previous checkpoint; dispose iteration scratch while keeping independent checkpoint ownership.
Preserve checkpoint state when moving back to a persistent continuation.
If no backend supports the required scoped reduction shape, auto placement returns to the existing row aggregation path; required placement and budget failures are not silently downgraded.

scenarios: Scalar and grouped one-shot backends receive an allocation scope on every execution.
Correct count/sum across 16 and 64 batches with identical peak reservations, proving no per-batch checkpoint accumulation for these fixed-state reductions.
Third-execution backend failure releases retained prior checkpoint and scratch.
Continuation-to-checkpoint-to-continuation transition preserves count, sum and median.
Binary input shape rejected by scoped vector reduction uses row counting correctly, with both routes explicitly observed and final reservations zero.

remaining: Other row fallback/stateful expression, parser and physical planning allocations remain under audit.
This closes the columnar fallback snapshot ownership gap, not the entire allocation matrix or total runtime heap contract.
Remote/cloud fallback execution and broader shape/aggregate scaling remain separate acceptance work.
